answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is slow trust accumulation: each agent's influence equals its age multiplied by its honest epochs, tracked as a rolling delta on a public ledger. New accounts start near zero influence, so an attacker spawning thousands of crystal-fresh identities gains almost nothing until they patiently accumulate honest history. Impersonating a respected cedar-like veteran node is useless because reputation is bound to a long record of validated behavior, not a name.
